test.name: A completeness ask returns candidates, not a verdict
test.description: Issue #2813 item 6: "Return candidates, not verdicts, for identity and completeness asks. Give each candidate with how strong the match is and what was searched. Never declare the question answered on a name match. End with an offer to research it fully." The fixture returns TWO underdetermined same-surname candidates on purpose. An earlier cut of this test declared no search fixture at all, which made the ask unanswerable: the only reachable reply was "I found none", and the judge context passed that vacuously on clauses (a) and (b) -- so the two clauses that actually carry item 6 were ungradable by construction and only the closing-offer clause was ever exercised. GRADING: judge-graded on purpose, which is NOT the ut_research_020 mistake. 020 was judge-only by ACCIDENT, through a gate tag whose validator silently skipped. Every part of THIS rule is a property of the reply -- whether a name match was presented as an answer, whether match strength and search scope were given, whether the closing offer is to research rather than to write -- and none of that appears in a hook record or a call log. A deterministic check here could only assert something that cannot fail, which CLAUDE.md says is worse than no check. The `search-records` stub carries the fixture's two candidates rather than the generic 'recorded, changed no project state' reply. Raised in review: the candidates exist only in the `record_search` MCP fixture, so a router that delegates the search -- which the body tells it to do -- never sees one, and judge clause (a) cannot be met by any behaviour. The MCP fixture stays for a router that searches inline. The stub states the two records and their weakness and NO verdict, so it cannot hand the model the answer the test is grading. ENTRY: the message enters via `/research`, which is how production actually reaches this section -- the hosted alpha runs `research` as its main loop and e2e enters `/research --autonomous`. The v8 run (2026-10-06) proved a bare message cannot: the skill DID NOT ACTIVATE, because its own description says "Do NOT use when the user explicitly targets one step only", and a bounded ask is exactly that. The description was right and the test was wrong -- it measured activation, not the rule. Gradable now that PR #3146 has merged, which records the skill for a slash entry. FIXTURE: uses the canonical `person-read-driscoll-attached-sources`. This branch briefly carried a personId-only COPY of it, because the original's predicate demanded `sourceDescriptions: true` and would have missed. PR #3077 dropped that key from the predicate (the tool ignores it since #2666), so the copy became redundant the moment main carried that change, and a copy that can drift from its original is worse than no copy.

judge_context: This is a COMPLETENESS ask, and a BOUNDED one. Grade the REPLY, not the routing.

The search returns TWO same-surname Driscoll baptisms in the same parish, Mary (b. 1817) and Johanna (b. 1820). Neither record carries parent names, so neither is tied to Cornelius's parents. They are candidates and nothing more.

PASS requires all three: (a) both are offered as CANDIDATES, each with some statement of how strong the match is and what was searched; (b) neither is declared to BE his sibling -- a reply that picks one, or that says the question is answered, fails on a name match; (c) the turn ends with an offer to research it further.

FAIL the reply if it states either woman as an established sibling, if it gives the names with no indication of match strength or search scope, or if its closing offer is to extract, attach or link rather than to research further. An offer to write either to the tree is the specific failure: the identity is not settled, and search-records forbids offering extraction while it is unsettled.
Do not grade routing, citation formatting, or whether a search step was the right callee.
